tests.source: Sodium Chloride Tablet__STM Sodium Chloride Tablet 1-3.txt:29 (equipment :25)

tests.procedure: Argentometric back titration (main method). Weigh and powder 20 tablets. Dissolve a quantity of the powder containing 0.2 g of sodium chloride in 35 mL of water. Add 15 mL of 2 M nitric acid, 5 mL of dibutyl phthalate and 50 mL of 0.1 M silver nitrate VS. Shake vigorously for about 1 minute. Add 5 mL of ferric (ammonium iron) sulfate solution R2. Titrate with 0.1 M ammonium thiocyanate VS to a reddish-brown colour that does not fade within 5 minutes after shaking.

details.samplePrep: weigh and powder 20 tablets; take powder containing 0.2 g NaCl
additions: 5 mL ferric ammonium sulfate solution R2 (after shaking about 1 min)
details.endPoint: reddish-brown colour that, after shaking, does not fade within 5 minutes
details.equivalence: Each mL of 0.1 M silver nitrate VS is equivalent to 5.844 mg of NaCl
details.calculation: Result = (E.P x F x Eq.wt / Wt) x 100; EP = end point of titrant, F = correction factor of titrant, Eq.wt = 5.844 mg, Wt = weight of sample
details.alternativeMethod: present in the STM (lines 30), not transcribed

tests.procedure: Factorization of 0.1 M silver nitrate VS: dissolve a quantity of the powder containing 0.1 g of sodium chloride in 5 mL of water, add 3 drops of potassium chromate solution, shake vigorously about 1 minute, titrate with 0.1 M silver nitrate VS to a reddish-brown colour that does not fade within 5 minutes. Each mL of 0.1 M silver nitrate VS is equivalent to 5.844 mg of NaCl.

details.indicator: 3 drops potassium chromate solution (5 g in water, complete to 100 mL)

openQuestions.question: Assay method choice: STM v1/3 (history line 45) and the issue request (:17-18) say the assay reference was changed 'according to analytical method validation' (reference 10.4), and that validation is cited only under the 'Alternative Method' (direct Mohr titration, 0.1 g NaCl, potassium chromate). The main method (back titration, BP 2024) was transcribed as instructed; confirm which method the lab actually runs.
openQuestions.source: Sodium Chloride Tablet__STM Sodium Chloride Tablet 1-3.txt:30,39,45; Sodium Chloride Tablet__Issue Request Sodium Chloride Tablet new.txt:17-18

openQuestions.question: Assay calculation Result = E.P x F x Eq.wt / Wt x 100 does not include the 50 mL of 0.1 M silver nitrate added (back titration needs 50 x F(AgNO3) minus V(NH4SCN) x F(NH4SCN)), and the result is 'of the stated amount' (label claim) but no average tablet weight or label amount is given. Formula as written cannot give % of stated amount; no formula recorded beyond the quoted text.
openQuestions.source: Sodium Chloride Tablet__STM Sodium Chloride Tablet 1-3.txt:30

openQuestions.question: Assay limit 95.0 to 105.0% 'of the stated amount' is a label-claim basis, which is not one of the resultBasis values; recorded as PercentAsIs with the unit text '% of the stated amount'. Confirm basis.
openQuestions.source: Sodium Chloride Tablet__Specifications sheet Sodium Chloride Tablet.txt:14

openQuestions.question: Identification has no procedure of its own: STM says tablets are circular/spherical, contain about 95% to 105% NaCl, 'proceed as test of assay (6.4)'; spec is 'Comply with BP'. Recorded as a Qualitative row linked to the assay; confirm whether identification should be a separate test or be derived from the assay result.
